cluster_protocol_history.1: openraft 0.9 — snapshot at POST /raft/install-snapshot, chunked stream {vote, meta, offset, data, done}; leader handoff at /raft/trigger-elect
cluster_protocol_history.2: openraft 0.10 — snapshot at POST /raft/snapshot, whole-snapshot (vote, meta, Vec<u8>); leader handoff at /raft/transfer-leader-msg. Bumped by commit 4a10c3d (2026-07-17). vote + append-entries stayed wire-compatible across this bump (measured, R625-S1); the snapshot path did not.
cluster_protocol_history.3: R706 (W294) — cluster secrets carry an ACCESS RULE. YubabaRequest::PutSecret and SecretRecord each gained `access: SecretAccess` (#[serde(default)] = deny-all). Nothing fails to PARSE in either direction, which is exactly why this needed a bump rather than a re-record: a mixed cluster is silently mis-authorized, not visibly broken. An epoch-2 node replicating an epoch-3 PutSecret drops the unknown `access` field on the floor and, having no check of its own, keeps serving that secret to ANY workload that names it — so the authorization guarantee R706 exists to create does not hold cluster-wide until every node is on 3. (The reverse direction is safe: an epoch-3 node applying an epoch-2 PutSecret defaults to deny-all and refuses, which is loud and re-fixable with `yah cloud secret put`.) Cheap moment to take: the fleet had zero cluster secrets and no node had a cluster KEK when this landed. CLUSTER_PROTOCOL is advertised on GET /health and in the signed release manifest — it is not a hard join gate — so this does not mechanically block a rolling upgrade; it makes the mixed window visible to the operator, which is the whole point here.
cluster_protocol_history.4: R732-F1 (W245) — tenant fencing epochs. `YubabaRequest` gained three variants (ClaimTenant, TransferTenant, RenewTenantLease), `YubabaResponse` gained `Tenant(TenantOutcome)`, and `YubabaState` gained `tenants: BTreeMap<TenantId, TenantOwnership>` (#[serde(default)]). The discriminator against BOTH prior precedents in this file: R706's `access` and R720-F1's `digest` added struct FIELDS, which serde tolerates in both directions (no deny_unknown_fields anywhere in this chain) — R706 was bumped only because a tolerated field made a mixed cluster silently mis-authorized, and R720-F1 was correctly NOT bumped. This change adds enum VARIANTS to the replicated command type, which is a different animal: `YubabaRequest` is externally tagged with no #[serde(other)] catch-all, so an epoch-3 node receiving a replicated ClaimTenant entry over AppendEntries gets `unknown variant "ClaimTenant"`, cannot apply it, cannot advance its state machine past that log index, and diverges. Verified by test rather than asserted from serde's documented behaviour: raft::tests::an_unknown_request_variant_fails_to_parse_which_is_why_r732_bumped_both_epochs, which also fails loudly if anyone later adds a catch-all variant and makes this entry untrue. The break is CONDITIONAL — a mixed cluster works normally until the first tenant claim is committed — but making that window visible to the operator is exactly what advertising the epoch on GET /health is for. Reverse direction is safe: an epoch-4 node reads every epoch-3 entry unchanged. Cheap moment taken, same reasoning as history "3": the tenants map does not exist before this change, so no fleet has a tenant ownership record and nothing is in flight during the roll.
cluster_protocol_history.5: R737-F1 (W246) — tenant PLACEMENT INTENT, separate from ownership. `YubabaRequest` gained two variants (SetTenantPlacement, ClearTenantPlacement), `YubabaState` gained `placement: BTreeMap<TenantId, TenantPlacement>` (#[serde(default)]), and `MemberInfo` + `YubabaRequest::SetMember` each gained `capacity: Option<NodeCapacity>` (#[serde(default)]). THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE SAME ONE R732-F1 RECORDED, and it is the variants alone that force this: `YubabaRequest` is externally tagged with no #[serde(other)] catch-all, so an epoch-4 node receiving a replicated SetTenantPlacement over AppendEntries gets `unknown variant "SetTenantPlacement"`, cannot apply it, cannot advance past that log index, and diverges. Pinned by raft::tests::an_unknown_request_variant_fails_to_parse_which_is_why_r732_bumped_both_epochs, which covers the mechanism rather than the specific variant name. THE FIELDS DID NOT NEED IT, checked rather than assumed. `capacity` is a tolerated struct field in both directions (the R720-F1 `digest` precedent, correctly NOT bumped), and the R706 hazard — a tolerated field that makes a mixed cluster silently WRONG rather than visibly broken — does not apply here. R706 bit because an old node dropped `access` and then served the secret to anybody. An old node dropping `capacity` records None, and None is defined as capacity-UNKNOWN, which YubabaState::node_headroom refuses to schedule onto. The degradation is fail-closed: the mixed window costs placement ONTO the un-upgraded nodes, never a placement that overcommits one. Same shape as R734-F5's region residual. NOTHING READS PLACEMENT YET — the scheduler is R737-F3. This ticket lands the state model and its publisher, so the mixed window has no behaviour to be wrong about beyond the divergence the variants already force.

state_epoch_history.1: openraft 0.9 storage-v1 on-disk raft log + snapshot layout
state_epoch_history.2: openraft 0.10 storage-v2 on-disk raft log + snapshot layout. Bumped by commit 4a10c3d (2026-07-17).
state_epoch_history.3: R732-F1 (W245) — tenant fencing epochs, disk side of the same change as cluster_protocol "4". NEW-READS-OLD holds: `tenants` is #[serde(default)], so an epoch-3 binary loads a pre-R732 snapshot with an empty map — which denies every write rather than assuming ownership it has no record of (pinned by raft::tests::pre_r732_snapshot_without_tenants_field_loads_owning_nothing). ROLL BACK is what breaks, and this axis explicitly claims it. The blocker is the LOG, not the snapshot: store.rs persists raft_log.json as serde_json over `BTreeMap<u64, Entry>` whose payload is the same `YubabaRequest` enum as the wire, and load reads that map whole — so a single retained (un-purged) ClaimTenant / TransferTenant / RenewTenantLease entry makes a downgraded epoch-2 binary fail to deserialize its own log at startup. It does not lose a feature; it does not start. The snapshot direction is fine both ways (YubabaState has no deny_unknown_fields, so an old binary silently drops the `tenants` key), and openraft does eventually purge applied entries — but a snapshot does not retire a log entry the moment it is applied, so there is always a window, and 'reversible only if you are lucky about purge timing' is not what this axis promises. This is the first state_epoch bump that is not an openraft storage migration; the criterion is the axis's own claim, not the shape of the precedents. Same cheap moment as the wire axis: no fleet log contains a tenant entry today, so a rollback taken before the first claim is still clean.
state_epoch_history.4: R737-F1 (W246) — same change, and it moves this axis for the LOG, not for the snapshot. The snapshot half is a non-event: `placement` on YubabaState and `capacity` on MemberInfo are both #[serde(default)], so an epoch-3 snapshot loads on the new binary declaring nothing and unschedulable, and a new snapshot loads on the old binary with the unknown fields dropped. What breaks is the ROLLBACK question this axis actually asks. `raft_log.json` is a BTreeMap<u64, Entry> of serde_json, and an Entry's payload is EntryPayload::Normal(YubabaRequest) — so a log that has ever carried a SetTenantPlacement cannot be deserialized by an epoch-3 binary at all, and the node does not start rather than starting wrong. Identical reasoning to R732-F1's entry on this axis; recorded again rather than cross-referenced because the next reader will be deciding about a different change and needs the mechanism, not a pointer.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING — cluster_protocol_surface re-recorded, the epoch stays 5. state_epoch is untouched and was already green: its recorded hash has matched the tree throughout, so nothing on the on-disk axis was ever in question here. This entry closes R829, which had the guard RED on committed main for a week and gated every CI push and every release-check run.
surface_rerecords.cause: TWO THINGS, and separating them is the whole finding. (1) THE MECHANICAL HALF: the value this replaces, 379ebab3…, never described any committed tree. It describes the surface as it stood at commit 8b35b0a9, but it was written into this file at 145b3f5e (2026-08-20) by R782's `--write`, two commits later. Shown mechanically rather than argued: holding the other four inputs at their (unchanged) state and sweeping lib.rs across the last 60 revisions, 8b35b0a9's lib.rs is the one and only revision that reproduces 379ebab3…. The asymmetry is the tell — R782 re-recorded BOTH axes in that run and state_epoch came out correct, and state_epoch is the axis with no lib.rs input. So at write time this shared working tree carried R782's own new raft/mod.rs beside a lib.rs that predated a peer's R605-F12 edit, and the later `sync` commit swept in both. (2) THE SEMANTIC HALF, which is what was actually never adjudicated: R605-F12 (`sovereign_role`). It is the only input that moved between 8b35b0a9 and 145b3f5e on this axis — `rust-items … fn raft_*`, 18f22799… -> 06b66ba6…. R782's verdict block reasons only about its own `rpo_bound` change and does not mention sovereign_role at all, so the compatibility call for R605-F12 on the wire axis is made here for the first time.
why_not_a_bump: IT IS THE R742-F1 SHAPE, EXACTLY — see the 2026-08-11 entry below, correctly re-recorded. Same two handlers, same mechanism, one more axis on the same gate: R742-F1 put a sovereign-GROUP gate on POST /raft/add-learner and a `sovereign_group` key on GET /raft/status; R605-F12 adds the ROLE (may this box hold a quorum seat) beside the group, read by the same `sovereign_group::judge` from the same two places.

NOTHING ON THE REPLICATION PATH MOVED. `SovereignRole` lives on `ServerState` (in-memory) and in the `/raft/status` response body; it is not a field of `YubabaRequest`, `YubabaResponse` or `YubabaState`, and raft/mod.rs, raft/network.rs and the `/raft/` route table are all byte-identical across this change (the mod.rs delta between those commits is R782's `rpo_bound`, adjudicated in the 2026-08-19 entry). Append-entries, vote, pre-vote and snapshot are unchanged, so an old-build voter and a new-build voter replicate together exactly as before. The openraft pin does not move.

THE OLD-PEER DIRECTION IS EXPLICITLY DEFAULTED, not accidentally tolerated. `sovereign_group::read_group` maps an absent `sovereign_role` key to `SovereignRole::Voter` (oss/yubaba/crates/yubaba/src/sovereign_group.rs:302), which is what declaring a group alone has always meant — so every daemon between R742-F1 and R605-F12, i.e. the entire current prod raft, is judged precisely as it was before the field existed. That is deliberate and documented at the site: refusing them would stop a stamped cluster growing until every member had been rolled, a strictly worse failure than the one the role guards.

NOT THE R706 HAZARD (a tolerated field that makes a mixed cluster silently WRONG). The role is only ever read by the node that DIALS `/raft/status`, never applied from replicated state, so an old node cannot act wrongly on it. Same reasoning the 2026-08-11 entry recorded for `sovereign_group` itself.

NEW BEHAVIOUR IS OPT-IN BY A FLAG THE OLD BUILD DOES NOT HAVE. The gate runs only on a daemon started with `--sovereign-group`; without it every path is byte-identical to epoch-5 behaviour, so upgrading a node changes nothing until an operator also changes its unit.
ROLLBACK IS FREE. Nothing is persisted — no log entry, no snapshot byte, no state-machine field — which is why state_epoch did not move and did not need to.
surface_rerecords.residual_risk: One window, already named at the code site and not introduced by this re-record: a box whose machine.toml says `non-voter` but whose daemon predates `--sovereign-role` answers "voter" and this gate admits it. `cloud::judge_join` reads the TOML and refuses it on the camp side, which is where operator-driven joins go, so the node-side gate is a backstop lagging a rollout rather than an unguarded path. It closes for a given group the moment its nodes carry the flag.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING on either axis — both hashes re-recorded, cluster_protocol stays 5 and state_epoch stays 4. The only input either axis touched is raft/mod.rs (in both surfaces), and the move on it is a plain new struct FIELD, not a variant — the R720-F1 `digest` / R734-F2 `capacity` shape, correctly not bumped, not the R732-F1 / R737-F1 enum-variant shape that was. The new `POST /mesh/rpo-report` route and its `mesh_rpo_report` handler (lib.rs) do not touch either lib.rs input: cluster_protocol's route-table slice only keeps lines containing the `/raft/` needle (this route is `/mesh/…`, same reason the earlier `/mesh/lease-renew` route didn't match), and its handler-set slice only keeps top-level fns named `raft_*` (this handler is `mesh_rpo_report`).
surface_rerecords.cause: R782 (W253 §7) — plumbing the streamer-RPO gate. `TenantPlacement` gained `rpo_bound: Option<Duration>` (#[serde(default)]) so the leader has a per-tenant target to read; the matching evidence-source half (`RpoWatermarkRegistry`, `POST /mesh/rpo-report`, `scheduler::spawn`'s new `rpo_registry` param) lives in lease_detector.rs/lib.rs/scheduler.rs, none of which are inputs to either axis — `judge_readiness`'s own arithmetic already shipped inert (R737-F2) and needed no epoch of its own then either.
why_not_a_bump: Field, not variant — the load-bearing discriminator this file has used since R720-F1. `TenantPlacement` is a struct carried inside `YubabaRequest::SetTenantPlacement` and inside `YubabaState.placement`; adding a field to it changes neither enum's tag set, so an old node's serde simply drops the unknown key on the way in and defaults it to `None` on the way out — no `unknown variant` failure, no divergence, no inability to apply a replicated entry.

R706 hazard checked, does not apply. An old (pre-R782) node dropping `rpo_bound` reads exactly the value it already read before this ticket: `None`, which `judge_readiness` documents as vacuously satisfied. It is not silently WRONG in the R706 sense (an old node did not gain a check it then evaluates incorrectly) — it is silently the SAME as before, which is the safe direction R720-F1 / R734-F2 already established for a tolerated field.

The reverse direction (old leader, new followers, or a downgrade) is the same non-event: an old leader never reads or writes `rpo_bound` at all, so the gate simply stays inert on that leader exactly as it was before R782 — a known, documented, and safe degradation (the underlying WAL->R2 durability the gate reasons about is unaffected; only the placement scheduler's extra caution is unavailable), not a data-loss path.

cluster_protocol's lib.rs slices (route lines containing `/raft/`, top-level `fn raft_*` items) are untouched by the new `/mesh/rpo-report` route or `mesh_rpo_report` handler — identical reasoning to the 2026-08-15 entry's `/mesh/lease-renew` precedent, restated because the same shape landed again.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING — cluster_protocol_surface re-recorded, the epoch stays 4. state_epoch is untouched: R742-F1 adds no type, no variant and no field to any replicated request or to YubabaState, and does not touch raft/mod.rs or raft/store.rs. On the wire axis it adds no route and no peer RPC payload — append-entries, vote, pre-vote, snapshot and write are byte-identical and the openraft pin does not move. What moved the hash is two `raft_*` handlers in lib.rs.
surface_rerecords.cause: R742-F1 (W305 §F1): the sovereign-group gate on POST /raft/add-learner. `raft_status` gained a `sovereign_group` key (this node's own --sovereign-group, emitted even when null); `raft_add_learner` gained a pre-membership gate that dials the prospective learner's /raft/status, refuses 409 on a cross-group or unestablishable group, 502 when the joiner cannot be asked at all, and reports `sovereign_group_judged` on success.
why_not_a_bump: A MIXED CLUSTER KEEPS WORKING UNCHANGED. Nothing on the replication, election or snapshot path moved, so an old-build voter and a new-build voter sit together exactly as before. The change is confined to one operator-driven membership verb and one operator-driven read.

THE NEW BEHAVIOUR IS OPT-IN BY A FLAG THE OLD BUILD DOES NOT HAVE. The gate runs only on a daemon started with --sovereign-group. Without it every response and every code path is byte-identical to epoch-4 behaviour, so upgrading a node changes nothing until an operator also changes its unit. That is also why this is not the shape of history "3": R706 changed what an existing replicated request MEANT, silently, with no operator action.

THE ADDITIVE FIELD IS IGNORABLE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. `sovereign_group` on /raft/status is a new JSON key an old reader drops; a new reader treats a missing key as Unsupported and a null as Undeclared, both of which it handles explicitly. Deliberately NOT the R706 hazard: there an old node silently mis-authorized because it dropped a field it had no check for. Here the field is only ever read by the node that DIALS, never applied from replicated state, so an old node cannot act wrongly on it — it can only fail to be asked, and the asking node treats that as a refusal, which is the safe direction.

REFUSING AN UN-ROLLED JOINER IS THE INTENDED OUTCOME, not a casualty of the change. A stamped leader refuses to add a learner whose build predates the field, because it cannot establish which blast radius that box belongs to. It costs a rolling upgrade nothing that matters: growth pauses, existing membership does not.

ROLLBACK IS SYMMETRIC AND FREE. Nothing is persisted — no log entry, no snapshot byte, no state-machine field — so rolling back to an epoch-4 build drops the flag and the gate together and leaves no residue to read. This is why state_epoch did not even move.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING on either axis — both hashes re-recorded, cluster_protocol stays 4 and state_epoch stays 3. R734-F5 introduces no new type, no new variant, no new field and no new route. It makes yubaba EMIT a request it never emitted before (YubabaRequest::SetMember, and RemoveMember on the removal path) and start populating MemberInfo.region, which R734-F2 added at these same epochs.
surface_rerecords.cause: R734-F5 (W247 §2): each node registers its own member row. New src/member_registration.rs (not a surface input); raft/store.rs gained read-only `members()` / `member(node_id)`; raft/mod.rs's MemberInfo gained `PartialEq, Eq`; lib.rs's `raft_status` grew a `members` section and `raft_remove_member` grew a region-spread clause, a row-clearing pass, and two new response keys (`stale_rows`, `spread_judged`).
why_not_a_bump: EMITTING an old variant is not a wire change. SetMember has existed since the first raft state machine and RemoveMember alongside it; both are already in every build's YubabaRequest. `region` is #[serde(default)] and was priced into BOTH axes by the R734-F2 re-record on 2026-08-10. An epoch-4 node that predates F5 applies a replicated SetMember carrying a region exactly as it always did. Contrast R732-F1, which had to bump because it added VARIANTS to the externally-tagged YubabaRequest, which an old node cannot parse and therefore cannot apply.

THE R706 HAZARD WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, and this is the one place this change differs from R734-F2. F2 could say `nothing reads MemberInfo.region`; that is no longer true — POST /raft/remove-member now refuses a removal that would leave one region holding a majority of the survivors. R706's `access` was a tolerated field that WAS bumped precisely because an enforcement path read it: an old node dropping it kept serving the secret with no check, silently defeating the guarantee. The shape that made that dangerous is absent here on three counts. (1) Nothing is dropped or defaulted in either direction — `region` round-trips through both builds; the pre-F5 node simply has no clause. (2) An old node's behaviour is IDENTICAL to the new node's own documented downgrade path (count clause only, when a survivor's region is unknown), so a mixed cluster produces an outcome the new code already produces on purpose rather than an unreachable one. (3) It is an operator-availability gate on an explicit, deliberate, one-at-a-time operator action, not a per-request authorization check on a data path — the failure mode is `a removal an upgraded node would have refused went through`, visible in the response body (`spread_judged: false` names it) and re-checkable, not a silent grant.

cluster_protocol's lib.rs slices are the `/raft/` route lines and the `fn raft_*` items. The route TABLE is untouched — no route added, removed or renamed. Two handler BODIES moved (raft_status, raft_remove_member) and both changes are additive JSON keys on operator-facing responses (`members`, `stale_rows`, `spread_judged`); no request type changed, so no peer sends or parses anything new. GET /raft/status is an operator surface, not a peer RPC — no node dials it.

state_epoch: on-disk bytes are unchanged in SHAPE. state_epoch 3 already prices in `members: BTreeMap<YubabaNodeId, MemberInfo>` with `region: Option<String>` (R734-F2). What changes is that real logs and snapshots now CONTAIN region values where before the map was empty. A downgraded pre-F2 binary reading such a log ignores the unknown `region` key (serde_json, no deny_unknown_fields anywhere in the chain) and applies the SetMember it can represent — no parse failure, no apply failure, and no divergence in any field that build knows about. `members()` / `member()` are read-only clones of an existing field, the same shape as the tenant_ownership() accessor re-recorded on 2026-08-10; `PartialEq, Eq` on MemberInfo derives no serialisation.
openraft pin unchanged at =0.10.0-alpha.30.
surface_rerecords.residual_risk: During a roll, the member map is INCOMPLETE rather than wrong: an un-rolled node publishes no row, so it is in raft membership with no region. Every consumer must treat a missing row as `unknown`, never as `no such node` — the removal gate does (it stands the spread clause down and reports spread_judged:false), and yubaba_test_harness::solo_node_unregistered exists so that branch stays tested. The gate is therefore only fully in force once every voter is rolled, which is the same shape as the R734-T1 pre-vote residual risk: it degrades toward the pre-F5 behaviour and never below it.

Enabling it against openraft 0.10.0-alpha.30 can strand a node as leader-per-peers and not-leader-per-itself, permanently — measured with tests/raft_membership_loop.rs under load: debug builds hit openraft's own `elect() requires leadership to be relinquished` debug_assert in 5 of 8 runs, release builds (where that assert compiles out) stranded a node on current_leader [None, Some(1), Some(1)] in roughly 40% of runs, still stuck after 75 seconds. Zero occurrences in 8 debug and 8 release control runs with the flag off. Cause is upstream: openraft's handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() guarded only on pre_candidate.is_none(), with no guard on leader.is_none(), where the real-vote path does guard. EVERYTHING ELSE FROM R734-T1 STAYS AND IS STILL LIVE — the /raft/pre-vote route, the RaftNetworkV2::pre_vote transport, and their tests. So the wire-compatibility reasoning in the T1 entry below still stands as written: the route exists and answers, and a peer that lacks it gets the documented 404-counts-as-a-grant degrade. What changed is only that yubaba does not currently SEND pre-votes, which makes a mixed cluster strictly simpler than the entry describes, never more complex.
surface_rerecords.residual_risk: Removing members is quorum-affecting by nature, which is why the handler gates on the surviving voter count before proposing anything (odd, non-empty). The gate cannot check region spread — openraft's node type is BasicNode{addr}, so raft membership carries no region, and R734-F2's MemberInfo.region is not written by anything in production yet. A removal can therefore still worsen quorum GEOGRAPHY (e.g. taking a 1-1-1 cluster to a 1-1 that is then refused for being even, or a 2-2-1 down to a 2-1-0 that is odd but region-lopsided) without being refused. Named in the handler's doc comment rather than left implicit; it closes when member rows carry regions.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING on either axis — both hashes re-recorded, cluster_protocol left at 4 and state_epoch left at 3
surface_rerecords.cause: R734-F2 (W247 §2). Quorum geography. `MemberInfo` gained `region: Option<String>` and `YubabaRequest::SetMember` gained the matching `region` field, both #[serde(default)] — that is raft/mod.rs, which is an input to BOTH surfaces, which is why both moved together for the first time since the openraft 0.10 bump. The wire axis also picked up the /raft/initialize handler, which now judges the founding voter set against the new ClusterPolicy::quorum_geography and refuses a violation with 400 before openraft writes anything.
why_not_a_bump: FIELD, NOT VARIANT — this is the whole verdict, and it is the exact discriminator history entry "4" (R732-F1) was written to establish. R732-F1 had to bump both axes because it added enum VARIANTS to `YubabaRequest`, which is externally tagged with no #[serde(other)]: an old node receiving a replicated ClaimTenant cannot parse it, cannot apply it, and diverges. `region` is a FIELD on an existing struct variant, and nothing in this chain carries #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] (re-grepped). So an old node replicating a new node's SetMember silently drops the key and applies the rest; a new node reading an old SetMember defaults it to None. Same shape as R720-F1's `digest`, which was correctly NOT bumped. Pinned by test rather than asserted: raft::tests::a_pre_r734_f2_set_member_still_applies_with_no_region.

NOT THE R706 HAZARD, and this is the question worth asking rather than the one worth assuming. R706's `access` was also a tolerated struct field, and it WAS bumped — because an old node that dropped it kept serving secrets an access rule was supposed to gate, so the guarantee silently did not hold cluster-wide. The test is whether any ENFORCEMENT path reads the new field. Here nothing does: QuorumGeography::judge is called by the /raft/initialize handler on the founding REQUEST PAYLOAD, at a moment when there is no cluster and no replicated state to consult. `MemberInfo.region` is recorded state, read by no gate. An old node dropping it therefore changes no decision anywhere, which is precisely what was untrue of `access`.

STATE_EPOCH, the rollback direction — the axis's own claim, checked in both directions by a_pre_r734_f2_snapshot_loads_untagged_and_a_downgrade_reads_a_tagged_one. New-reads-old: an untagged member row loads as region None. Roll BACK is what R732-F1 could not promise, because its blocker was the LOG (store.rs persists raft_log.json as serde_json over entries carrying the same YubabaRequest enum, so one retained un-purged ClaimTenant entry stops a downgraded binary from starting). A field is not a variant: a downgraded pre-R734-F2 binary parses a region-tagged SetMember log entry and a region-tagged member row in a snapshot, dropping the key both times. The downgrade is clean, so the axis's promise holds and this is a re-record.

THE /raft/initialize SHAPE CHANGE IS OPERATOR-FACING, NOT PEER-TO-PEER. This axis asks whether two BUILDS can sit in one raft cluster; /raft/initialize is called once, by an operator, on a node that is not yet in a cluster at all — no node ever dials it. Two builds' ability to exchange append-entries, vote, pre-vote, snapshot and transfer-leader is untouched. The request also stays backward-compatible on purpose: `members` accepts both the pre-region `id -> "host:port"` form and the tagged object form (serde untagged), so an old operator script reaches the POLICY refusal with an actionable message about region tags rather than a 422 that reads like a JSON typo. Pinned by tests/raft_quorum_geography.rs::the_pre_region_request_shape_reaches_the_policy_refusal_not_a_parse_error.

surface_rerecords.residual_risk: A BEHAVIOUR change an operator must know about, though not a compatibility one: under the fleet profile, `raft init` on a multi-voter cluster now REFUSES an untagged founding set, where before it succeeded. That is the deliverable rather than a side effect — W247's whole point is that an untagged bootstrap is how a cluster ends up with a quorum that dies with one datacenter — but a runbook that founds a fleet cluster without `@region` suffixes will now fail, and the fix is to add them from .yah/infra/machines/<name>.toml. A cluster-of-one and every rig-profile cluster are unaffected. Separately: nothing in production writes `MemberInfo.region` yet, because nothing writes SetMember at all (grep: the only callers are tests) — so a mixed cluster has no region rows to disagree about, and the field is currently a data model for R736-T3 and R737-F1 plus the founding-time check, not live fleet state.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING — hash re-recorded, cluster_protocol left at 4
surface_rerecords.cause: R734-T1 (W247). Pre-Vote turned on. Three coupled edits: `enable_pre_vote: Some(true)` in RaftTiming::to_openraft_config (cluster_policy.rs, not itself a surface input), `RaftNetworkV2::pre_vote` implemented in raft/network.rs, and a new POST /raft/pre-vote route + `fn raft_pre_vote` handler in lib.rs. The latter two are why this axis moved; state_epoch stayed GREEN and needed no action, correctly — store.rs is untouched and raft/mod.rs's non-comment content did not change, because a Pre-Vote never produces a log entry and so has no on-disk existence at all.
why_not_a_bump: OLD DIALS NEW: an old node never sends a Pre-Vote. openraft's `enable_pre_vote` defaults to None and `get_enable_pre_vote()` reads None as false, so a pre-R734-T1 build has the feature off and its election path is byte-for-byte the one it always had. The new route is additive and simply never dialed by it. Every route an old node DOES dial — /raft/vote, /raft/append-entries, /raft/snapshot, /raft/transfer-leader-msg — is unchanged in path, payload type, and semantics.

NEW DIALS OLD: this is the direction that needed a deliberate decision, and it is handled in the client rather than left to chance. openraft counts only an affirmative `Ok(granted)` toward the Pre-Vote quorum — an `Err` is never a grant, by design, so that an isolated node cannot synthesize a quorum from its own unreachable peers. A naive implementation would therefore turn the old peer's 404 into a non-grant, and a new node could then fail to assemble a pre-vote quorum and never campaign: a mixed cluster that goes leaderless after a leader failure, which WOULD have been a bump (and a nasty one, since nothing in the logs looks like a failure). YubabaNetwork::pre_vote instead treats HTTP 404 specifically as a grant — the peer answered, it is reachable, its build just has no route — which is exactly the degrade openraft's own default `pre_vote` impl provides for a network that has not implemented the RPC. A connect failure still returns Err, so the isolated-node protection is untouched. Verified by test, not asserted: raft::network::tests::a_404_from_a_pre_r734_peer_counts_as_a_grant, a_real_refusal_survives_the_404_fallback (an honest refusal is not rewritten into a grant by an over-broad fallback), and an_unreachable_peer_is_an_error_not_a_grant.

NO NEW WIRE TYPES. /raft/pre-vote carries VoteRequest and VoteResponse — the identical types /raft/vote has always carried. This is not the R732-F1 shape (new enum variants on the replicated command type, which an old node cannot parse and so cannot apply, diverging its state machine); nothing here is replicated at all. A Pre-Vote is a question, and handling one persists no vote, changes no term, and writes no log entry — pinned by tests/raft_pre_vote.rs::a_pre_vote_probes_without_persisting_while_a_real_vote_commits, which sends the SAME request to both routes and reads the responder's term back after each.
openraft pin unchanged at =0.10.0-alpha.30.
surface_rerecords.residual_risk: During a mixed window, a new node's Pre-Vote grants from old peers are free grants, so Pre-Vote's protection is weaker than in a fully-rolled cluster. It degrades toward the pre-R734-T1 behaviour and never below it — a free grant can only let a candidate proceed to the real election, which is what it would have done unconditionally before this change, and the real vote still respects the leader lease. So there is no window in which the fleet is worse off than it was; there is a window in which the new protection is only partial. Fully realised once every voter is rolled.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING — hashes re-recorded, cluster_protocol left at 3, state_epoch left at 2
surface_rerecords.cause: R720-F1 (W294) / R625-B6. `digest: Option<Vec<u8>>` added to SecretRecord (raft/mod.rs) and to YubabaRequest::PutSecret, both #[serde(default)]. raft/store.rs's cluster_secret_index() gained a fourth (digest, hex-encoded) column plus a local hex_encode helper.
why_not_a_bump: Unlike R706's `access` (history "3"), digest carries NO enforcement path — nothing anywhere gates a decision on its presence or absence. It is a read-only, keyed diagnostic value surfaced on GET /secrets purely for `yah cloud secret status` (R720-T2) to compare a camp's declaration against what the fleet is serving. Its own doc comment states the contract: `None` means 'predates digests', never 'matches' — so a node that drops the unknown field, or one reading a record that never had one, both land on the SAME documented state (unknown(pre-digest)), not a silent lie and not a security bypass. That is the structural difference from access, whose absence changed what a mount-time gate actually enforced.

Wire direction (cluster_protocol), re-verified by reading network.rs and lib.rs rather than assumed: every raft RPC (append-entries, vote, snapshot) goes over reqwest .json()/axum Json<T> — serde_json IS the wire format, confirming R625-S1's finding still holds. No #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] anywhere in the SecretRecord / PutSecret / YubabaRequest chain (grepped). An epoch-3 node receiving an epoch-4 leader's replicated PutSecret silently drops the unknown `digest` key; an epoch-4 node receiving an epoch-3 leader's PutSecret defaults digest to None via #[serde(default)]. Every node in the cluster applies the identical replicated log bytes in the identical order — openraft's consistency model is 'same log, same order, same apply()', not per-node content negotiation — so there is no state-machine divergence risk here, only a per-node representation gap that IS what None already means.

Disk direction (state_epoch), same method: store.rs persists both raft_log.json and raft_state.json via serde_json::to_string — the same self-describing format as the wire, confirmed by reading the actual persist_log/persist_vote code and the module's own doc comment, not inferred from convention. An epoch-4 binary reads an epoch-3 snapshot/log (digest absent -> None); an epoch-3 binary reads an epoch-4 snapshot/log (digest present, silently dropped — the old binary never had a use for it). Neither direction errors, and rollback is genuinely reversible: a downgraded node keeps serving every existing secret exactly as before, just without the drift-check precision digest adds.

raft/store.rs's contribution to this axis's hash is the same shape the 2026-08-03 entry already recorded for cluster_secret_index() itself: a read-only accessor over the secrets map, in the hash only because the whole file is a surface input, touching no serialisation path. This change extends that same accessor with one more hex-encoded column.

surface_rerecords.residual_risk: None security-relevant, unlike R706's access-rule gap — no authorization or mount decision reads digest. It self-heals the next time that secret is re-shipped with `yah cloud secret put` from a fully-rolled camp.
